    use Capture::Tiny qw(capture);
    my ($o, $e) = capture { binmode(STDOUT, q{:utf8}); binmode(STDERR, q{:utf8});
                            print "STDOUT:Hi! \x{263a}\n"; print STDERR "STDERR:Hi! \x{263a}\n" };
    # ords of $o
    perl 5.40.3: 53 54 44 4f 55 54 3a 48 69 21 20 263a a   (CHARACTERS: the
                 captured STDOUT is read back through the handle's :utf8 layer)
    PCL:         ... 20 e2 98 ba a                          (UTF-8 BYTES)
    ($e is bytes in both: perl reads STDERR's capture without the layer.)

scratch/s517a/pr/ct.pl.  Capture::Tiny reads PerlIO::get_layers(*STDOUT) and
re-applies them to the capture file (_relayer / _copy_std); PCL's answer to
get_layers or its binmode on the reopened tmpfile handle loses the :utf8.
Probe get_layers on a :utf8 STDOUT first.


=== DONE (s521b, 2026-10-18, commit 53f472fd -- #139 part (b), the RULED shape) ===
PerlIO::get_layers exists (a core sub, marked defined): the layers PCL APPLIES -- `unix perlio` + `utf8` (UTF-8 discipline) or
`encoding(NAME) utf8`, derived from the handle's one external format; `scalar` for an in-memory handle; () for closed / unopened /
non-handle; scalar context = top entry.  `:pop` takes off the top layer (a UTF-8 flag goes WITH perlio -> `unix`, octets), `:perlio`
puts the base back; the pop count is a list-only per-stream state (*p-layer-pops*).  perl's table (scratch/s521b/pr/gl1.pl):
fresh `unix perlio`; :utf8 `unix perlio utf8`; binmode/:raw `unix perlio`; :encoding(UTF-8) `unix perlio encoding(utf-8-strict) utf8`
(PCL `unix perlio utf8` -- not-supported); pop after :utf8 `unix`; pop again (); closed/unopened (); "STDIN" string `unix perlio`;
scalar ctx `perlio`; in-memory `scalar`; 42 / [] ().  BAR: the capture probe (scratch/s521b/pr/ct1.pl) = perl (13 13, 263a);
Capture-Tiny 02 03 07 08 12 13 14 15 20-24 one-file runs: 682 #3326 rows + 438 #3327 rows + 11 *PLAN* leave by edit; 19-relayering
5/0 in 19 s (no hang); Path-Tiny digest.t 7/0 (its *FILE* row leaves).  Guard Pl/t/io-layers-01.t rows 40-41 (FAIL on ed8a4504; the
